status: PROPOSAL ONLY. READ-ONLY AUDIT. No class, enum, migration, route, controller, model, event, notification or test was created. No Creative code exists: 0 classes, 0 routes, 0 tables, 0 migrations, 0 tests. Every state set below is a RECOMMENDATION, not a description of existing behaviour.
classification: CURRENT_FACT for every entry in reusable_state_transition_patterns_in_current_codebase and every current-code citation. RECOMMENDATION for every proposed Creative state, transition, actor, side effect and event. OPEN_DECISION wherever a transition rule cannot be derived from evidence. ARCHITECTURE_DOCUMENT for the rule citations. INFERENCE for reasoning that follows from the verified facts but is not itself stated anywhere.
method: Read every existing state vocabulary in the codebase end to end: BookingStatus, PaymentStatus, App\Models\Booking, App\Models\Payment, App\Models\Partner, App\Models\PartnerCommission, App\Models\ScreenProviderSettlement, App\Models\BookingMedia, App\Models\ScreenProviderEnquiry, and the enquiry status columns in the migrations.

Read every existing transition site: app/Services/BookingWorkflowService.php, app/Services/SettlementService.php, app/Http/Controllers/PartnerApprovalController.php, app/Http/Controllers/BookingController.php, app/Http/Controllers/AdminManualBookingController.php, app/Http/Controllers/Api/BookingEngineController.php.
Searched for any generic state-machine abstraction (classes, traits, interfaces, composer packages). Result recorded verbatim in abstract_state_machine_availability.
Diffed the BookingStatus enum against the Booking model's STATUS_ constants by reflection, to measure enum/model drift exactly rather than by inspection.
Invented no business rule. Where a limit, window, threshold, penalty, actor set or accrual trigger is not derivable, the entry is OPEN_DECISION and states what is missing.

classification_legend.CURRENT_FACT: Verified from source code on 2026-09-26, with file:line evidence.
classification_legend.ARCHITECTURE_DOCUMENT: Defined by docs/architecture/ARCHITECTURE_RULES.md or root AGENTS.md.
classification_legend.INFERENCE: Reasonably inferred from the implementation or from relationships between artefacts.
classification_legend.RECOMMENDATION: Proposed target design. Not implemented. No enum, class, table or route was written.
classification_legend.OPEN_DECISION: Cannot be determined from available evidence; requires a product or architecture decision. The missing information is stated exactly.

reading_rules: Every state in every lifecycle is a RECOMMENDATION. There is no Creative code to describe.

No percentage, commission rate, limit, window, deadline, penalty, tax, currency-support statement or minimum amount appears anywhere in this artifact. Where such a value would be needed, the field is OPEN_DECISION.
'actor' names a ROLE (from artifact 13 section 5), not a person. Where the correct role is itself undecided, the actor is OPEN_DECISION.
'authorization_basis' names a permission string proposed in artifact 13 section 5, or a policy, or an OPEN_DECISION. No permission string here is seeded today.
database_change describes the row the RECOMMENDED transition would write. No such column or table exists.

global_conventions.enum_backed_status_columns: Every Creative status column is string(50) (or narrower where the vocabulary is small) cast to a PHP backed enum. This follows the dominant existing convention: database/migrations/2026_06_15_000001_create_screen_provider_enquiries_table.php:17 uses string(20), database/migrations/2026_09_01_000001_create_screen_provider_settlements_table.php:21 uses string default 'generated', and app/Domain/Booking/Enums/BookingStatus.php is a backed enum. DB-level ENUM is used nowhere in the Creative blueprint.
global_conventions.single_transition_owner: Each lifecycle has exactly ONE transition owner. This is already the case for Booking (app/Services/BookingWorkflowService.php:41) and partially for settlements (app/Services/SettlementService.php). The known anti-pattern to avoid is the Booking enum/model drift documented in booking_status_enum_model_drift below, which exists precisely because two owners exist.
global_conventions.no_generic_framework: No state-machine library or framework is to be introduced. See abstract_state_machine_availability and verdict.
global_conventions.guards_not_controllers: Every transition is guarded in the domain/service layer and throws a domain exception on an illegal transition. HTTP status mapping happens only in the exception's render() method, exactly as app/Domain/Booking/Exceptions/InvalidBookingStateException.php:11-18 already does. Controllers must not contain transition logic (ARCHITECTURE_RULES Rule 1, AGENTS.md section 6).
global_conventions.one_activity_log_per_transition: Every transition writes one activity_logs row (App\Models\ActivityLog already exists and is used for this, e.g. app/Http/Controllers/Api/RoleController.php:40-49). Append-only, matching booking_activities.
global_conventions.immutable_financial_records: creator_earnings rows are never updated to a new status in a way that destroys history: a reversal is a NEW row with a negative amount linked by reverses_earning_id (AGENTS.md section 10, 09-creative-database-target-schema-blueprint.json:574).
global_conventions.idempotency: Any transition that writes money must be safe to retry. 09-...json:563 already recommends UNIQUE(project_id, earning_type) as a double-credit backstop. There is no request-level idempotency key anywhere in the current codebase (artifact 14 section 10.1).

open_decisions.missing_information: A product decision, and the artifacts conflict. 09-...json:523 proposes is_public boolean default true (i.e. no moderation queue), while artifact 13 section 5.4 proposes a creative.reviews.moderate permission (i.e. a moderation queue). Both cannot be the design. Unresolved.

open_decisions.question: Does a creator's rating have any commercial consequence — rate, ranking, or visibility?
open_decisions.missing_information: A product rule. No ranking or rating-weighted behaviour exists anywhere in the current marketplace, and none is proposed here.

lifecycles.name: Earnings
lifecycles.state_set_provenance: The vocabulary deliberately mirrors the two closest existing financial lifecycles, both of which are real and verified: App\Models\PartnerCommission::STATUS_* (pending, approved, paid, cancelled, refunded) at app/Models/PartnerCommission.php:52-56, and App\Models\ScreenProviderSettlement::STATUS_* (draft, generated, approved, paid, cancelled) at app/Models/ScreenProviderSettlement.php:17-21, whose transitions are actually driven at app/Services/SettlementService.php:93 (generated), :150 (approved), :183 (paid), :231 (cancelled).

states.actor: RECOMMENDATION: system, on the accrual trigger
states.authorization_basis: RECOMMENDATION: no user permission; the accrual is a system consequence of another lifecycle transition. The accrual trigger is UNDEFINED — see OD-SM-09.
side_effects: RECOMMENDATION: the amount is snapshotted from the project's agreed terms at this moment, never recomputed later (AGENTS.md section 10)
states.database_change: RECOMMENDATION: INSERT creator_earnings row (status = 'pending') with gross_amount, platform_commission_rate, platform_commission_amount, creator_net_amount, currency, exchange_rate_used. UNIQUE(project_id, earning_type) is MANDATORY per 09-...json:563 as a double-credit backstop.
states.notification: RECOMMENDATION: earning-available notice to the creator
states.financial_effect: OPEN_DECISION: THE AMOUNT. The gross, the platform share, the creator net, the currency and any tax are all undefined. 09-...json:568-575 defines the COLUMNS and the invariant gross_amount = platform_commission_amount + creator_net_amount, but no value, no rate, no currency-support list and no tax rule exists in any source. NONE is proposed here. This artifact deliberately contains no percentage.

states.authorization_basis: RECOMMENDATION: creative.earnings.approve. NOTE: artifact 13 section 5.6 records that no finance role exists, so this permission currently has no role that can hold it independently of creative.payouts.approve — which means separation of duties is not yet expressible (OD-AUTH-05).
side_effects: RECOMMENDATION: the amount becomes eligible for payout
states.notification: RECOMMENDATION: approval notice
states.financial_effect: none — approval records a decision, it does not move money

states.actor: RECOMMENDATION: finance, as part of a payout
side_effects: RECOMMENDATION: the earning is attached to a payout via payout_id (09-...json:542)
states.database_change: RECOMMENDATION: UPDATE creator_earnings.status = 'released', released_at, payout_id. 09-...json:575 states the invariant: the sum of released earnings for a creator must never exceed the sum of their approved earnings.
states.event: RECOMMENDATION: modelled on app/Support/Events/Notifications/PaymentReceived.php (used for the paying side)
states.notification: RECOMMENDATION: payment-released notice to the creator
states.financial_effect: MONEY LEAVES THE PLATFORM. OPEN_DECISION: the payout mechanism itself is undefined — bank transfer, gateway disbursal, or manual. Missing information: the disbursal mechanism, the settlement schedule, and the failure/retry behaviour. No mechanism is proposed.

side_effects: MANDATORY per AGENTS.md section 10 and 09-...json:574: a reversal is a NEW row with a negative creator_net_amount linked via reverses_earning_id. It is NEVER an UPDATE or a DELETE of the original row.
states.database_change: RECOMMENDATION: INSERT a new creator_earnings row with status = 'reversed' and a negative amount, reverses_earning_id pointing at the original. The original row is left untouched and remains 'released' or 'approved'.
states.notification: RECOMMENDATION: reversal notice to the creator with the reason
states.financial_effect: MONEY IS RECLAIMED. The reversal amount must be derived from the original SNAPSHOT, not recomputed from current terms. OPEN_DECISION: who may trigger a reversal, in which states, and whether a reversal is permitted after the money has left the platform. Missing information: the policy.

states.actor: RECOMMENDATION: system, on the pre-approval path only
states.authorization_basis: RECOMMENDATION: no user permission. RECOMMENDATION: a cancellation of an UNRELEASED earning is a state change on the pending row; a reversal of a RELEASED earning is a compensating record. The two must not be conflated.
states.database_change: RECOMMENDATION: UPDATE creator_earnings.status = 'cancelled', cancelled_at (permitted only while status = 'pending' or 'approved')
states.notification: RECOMMENDATION: notice to the creator
states.financial_effect: none, PROVIDED the earning was never released. If it was released, 'cancelled' is forbidden and 'reversed' is mandatory.

payout_lifecycle_note.statement: A payout is a SEPARATE lifecycle from an earning. The existing repository already models exactly this split twice — App\Models\PartnerCommission (pending/approved/paid/cancelled/refunded) and App\Models\ScreenProviderSettlement (draft/generated/approved/paid/cancelled, driven at app/Services/SettlementService.php:93/150/183/231) — so Creative should follow suit rather than collapsing payout state into the earning.
payout_lifecycle_note.caveat: OPEN_DECISION: the payout minimum, the cadence, the disbursal mechanism, and whether a payout may be requested below the minimum are all undefined (OD-SM-16). 10-existing-table-reuse-analysis.json:1237 proposes a settings key creative.payout_minimum, but naming a key presupposes the rule, and the rule does not exist.

open_decisions.question: What are the earning amounts, the platform share, the creator net, the supported currencies and the tax treatment?
open_decisions.missing_information: A finance policy. NO source in this repository or in any audit artifact states any of these. This artifact contains no percentage, no currency list and no tax rule, and none may be inferred from the existing partner commission or screen provider settlement values, which are for different commercial relationships.

open_decisions.question: What is the payout minimum, the cadence, and the disbursal mechanism?
open_decisions.missing_information: A finance and operations policy. The existing repository pays screen providers through app/Services/SettlementService.php, but that is a different commercial relationship and its mechanism does not transfer automatically.

open_decisions.question: Who may reverse a released earning, in which states, and is reversal permitted after disbursement?
open_decisions.missing_information: An internal-control policy. AGENTS.md section 10 mandates the compensating-record mechanism but not the authorisation or the permitted states.

reusable_state_transition_patterns_in_cu.purpose: Every lifecycle below was read in full. This section exists so that the Creative design is built from what the codebase already does, not from what a state-machine library would do.

patterns.name: Booking.status
patterns.side_effect_on_reject: app/Services/BookingWorkflowService.php:53-56 — a reason is written into sold_out_reason, but ONLY when the target is rejected.
patterns.exposed_as: POST /api/v2/bookings/{id}/transition, body {"status": "required|string", "reason": "nullable|string"}, handled at app/Http/Controllers/Api/BookingEngineController.php:124-136. The controller performs NO state validation itself — it delegates to the service at :131.

important_defect.detail: App\Models\Booking declares 13 STATUS_ constants (app/Models/Booking.php:208-220): draft, payment_pending, payment_failed, media_review_pending, pending_approval, approved, rejected, scheduled, running, completed, cancelled, expired, refunded. The BookingStatus enum declares only 8 (draft, pending_approval, approved, rejected, scheduled, running, completed, cancelled). Five model values have NO enum case: payment_pending, payment_failed, media_review_pending, expired, refunded. Verified by reflection, not by eye.
important_defect.consequence: app/Services/BookingWorkflowService.php:45 uses $this->allowedTransitions[$currentStatus] ?? []. A booking whose status is any of the 5 unmapped values resolves to an EMPTY allowed list, so EVERY transition on it throws InvalidBookingStateException. The guard is fail-closed — which is the safe failure direction — but it means a booking in payment_pending is untransitionable through the workflow service.
important_defect.also: app/Models/Booking.php $casts (line 142 onward) does NOT cast status, so $booking->status is a raw string. The service defensively handles both at line 43.
important_defect.lesson_for_creative: Two owners of a status vocabulary (enum + model constants) produced a silent 5-state gap. Creative must have exactly ONE owner per vocabulary, and the enum must be exhaustive over every value the column can hold.

patterns.name: Payment.status
patterns.owner: app/Services/PaymentService.php and app/Services/RefundService.php (write sites); no single transition guard exists

two_distinct_vocabularies.legacy_razorpay_set: STATUS_PENDING, STATUS_VERIFICATION_PENDING, STATUS_PAID, STATUS_FAILED, STATUS_REFUNDED, STATUS_PARTIALLY_REFUNDED (app/Models/Payment.php:57-62)
two_distinct_vocabularies.note: app/Domain/Payment/PaymentStatus.php:12-27 documents both sets explicitly and states at :15-17: 'it is deliberately NOT an independent enum and it does NOT introduce a new state machine. No transition is enforced here; the existing services remain the transition owners.'

patterns.additional_vocabularies: A separate verification column vocabulary (VERIFICATION_PENDING / VERIFICATION_VERIFIED / VERIFICATION_FAILED, app/Models/Payment.php:64-66) and a separate refund_status vocabulary (REFUND_NONE / REFUND_PENDING / REFUND_PROCESSED / REFUND_FAILED, :68-72). FOUR status vocabularies on one financial record.
patterns.guard: NONE. There is no transition graph. Enforcement is by ad-hoc preconditions inside controllers: app/Http/Controllers/PaymentController.php:53-55 refuses when $booking->status !== Booking::STATUS_PAYMENT_PENDING, returning errorResponse('Booking is not in payment pending status.', 422).
patterns.lesson_for_creative: A financial record with four parallel status vocabularies and no transition guard is harder to reason about than one vocabulary with an enforced graph. Creative should not copy this. The positive lesson is the honesty of the comment at app/Domain/Payment/PaymentStatus.php:15-17, which explicitly refuses to pretend a state machine exists.

patterns.name: booking_media.review_status
patterns.owner: app/Http/Controllers/BookingController.php (write sites); the booking booking flow guards at the booking level, not the media level
patterns.column: database/migrations/2026_09_16_103654_add_review_fields_to_booking_media_table.php:12 — string('review_status')->default('pending'), with reviewed_by FK to users (nullOnDelete), reviewed_at, rejection_reason, and an index on review_status
patterns.graph: NOT WRITTEN DOWN ANYWHERE. There is no allowedTransitions array for review_status. The states are only ever set, never guarded.
write_sites: app/Http/Controllers/BookingController.php:1259 — 'review_status' => BookingMedia::REVIEW_APPROVED is set at 1223 and rejection at 1259 with the reason
patterns.guard_at_the_parent_level: app/Http/Controllers/BookingController.php:315 — errorResponse('Booking is not in a reviewable status.', 422). This is a BOOKING-state guard applied before a MEDIA review action, not a media-state guard.
patterns.events: app/Support/Events/Notifications/MediaUploaded.php, MediaApproved.php, MediaRejected.php all exist and are dispatched around these actions.
patterns.lesson_for_creative: This is the single closest structural analogue to a Creative delivery review, and it is the weakest of the existing lifecycles: no transition graph, no guard, states reachable from any prior state. Creative deliveries MUST have a written graph and a guard. The parts worth copying are the column design (status + reviewed_by + reviewed_at + reason, all present, with the actor recorded) and the event trio.

patterns.name: Partner approval (partner-applications)
patterns.vocabulary_owner: app/Models/Partner.php:14-18 — STATUS_PENDING 'pending', STATUS_UNDER_REVIEW 'under_review', STATUS_APPROVED 'approved', STATUS_REJECTED 'rejected', STATUS_INACTIVE 'inactive'
patterns.graph: NOT WRITTEN DOWN. Enforcement is by inline precondition checks in the controller: app/Http/Controllers/PartnerApprovalController.php:23 refuses approval unless in [STATUS_PENDING, STATUS_UNDER_REVIEW], returning 400 'Only pending or under review partners can be approved.'; :47 refuses rejection of an approved partner with 400; :69 sets STATUS_UNDER_REVIEW.
patterns.note_on_status_code: These guards return 400, not 422. That differs from the Booking precedent (422) — the codebase is not consistent about which status signals an illegal transition.
patterns.lesson_for_creative: This is the ONLY existing approval lifecycle with a review stage, and it is the closest analogue to LC-CREATOR. The vocabulary (pending, under_review, approved, rejected, inactive) is a reasonable shape to mirror. The guard style — inline in a controller — is not: Creative should use a written graph plus a domain exception, as RST-01 does, and must pick ONE status code for illegal transitions.

patterns.name: Screen-provider enquiry approval
patterns.verdict: This is a single-status lead record, NOT a lifecycle. It has a status column, an assigned_to FK (line 18) and internal_notes (line 19), which makes it a work-queue flag rather than a state machine. The identical pattern appears in product_enquiries (database/migrations/2026_07_01_000002_create_product_enquiries_table.php:18) and contact_enquiries (database/migrations/2026_07_15_000001_create_contact_enquiries_table.php:17).
patterns.lesson_for_creative: Do NOT model a Creative brief as a lead record. Three separate tables in this repository use a bare status defaulting to 'new' with no lifecycle, and that pattern is appropriate only for an inbound enquiry with no internal stages. A Creative brief has a buyer, a discovery phase, proposals, and a possible project — the lead pattern is far too thin.

patterns.name: Screen-provider settlement and partner commission (financial lifecycles)
patterns.vocabulary_owner: app/Models/ScreenProviderSettlement.php:17-21 — STATUS_DRAFT 'draft', STATUS_GENERATED 'generated', STATUS_APPROVED 'approved', STATUS_PAID 'paid', STATUS_CANCELLED 'cancelled'. Also App\Models\PartnerCommission.php:52-56 — STATUS_PENDING 'pending', STATUS_APPROVED 'approved', STATUS_PAID 'paid', STATUS_CANCELLED 'cancelled', STATUS_REFUNDED 'refunded'.
patterns.graph: NOT WRITTEN DOWN as a data structure, but the transitions ARE ordered and service-owned: app/Services/SettlementService.php:93 writes 'generated', :150 writes 'approved', :183 writes 'paid', :231 writes 'cancelled'.
patterns.derived_predicates: app/Models/ScreenProviderSettlement.php:114 (isEditable for draft/generated), :119 (isGenerated), :124 (isApproved), :129 (isPayable — !in_array(status, [PAID, CANCELLED])). These are the closest thing in the codebase to transition guards, but they are state PREDICATES, not edge guards: they cannot reject an illegal from-to pair.
patterns.known_defect: screen_provider_settlements has NO currency column (09-creative-database-target-schema-blueprint.json:20 records this explicitly as 'a defect Creative must not copy').
patterns.lesson_for_creative: Two things to copy and one to avoid. COPY: (a) the two-lifecycle split between an accrual record and a payout record, which Creative maps to creator_earnings + creator_payouts; (b) the paid/cancelled terminal pair and the isPayable predicate, which is a cheap and useful read-side guard. AVOID: the absence of a currency column, and the absence of edge guards.

patterns.name: Booking expiry (scheduled, not state-machine-driven)
patterns.finding: app/Models/Booking.php:219 declares STATUS_EXPIRED = 'expired', which is NOT a BookingStatus enum case. The expiry is driven by a scheduled console command, not by a transition guard. Per AGENTS.md section 16, three live scheduled commands (rewards:expire, bookings:expire-pending, currency:sync-rates) were once flagged as removable by a purely lexical scan.
patterns.lesson_for_creative: Any Creative lifecycle that includes a TIME-BOUND transition needs a scheduled command, and that command must be registered and verified (AGENTS.md section 16) rather than assumed. If Creative has an acceptance window (OD-SM-11) or a brief deadline (OD-SM-03), each implies a scheduled job that must be framework-registration verified.

evidence: No class, trait or interface named *StateMachine* or *StateMachine* exists anywhere in app/, tests/ or config/ — a case-insensitive content search for 'statemachine' and 'state_machine' returns zero matches.

Only 3 PHP enums exist in the entire application: app/Enums/AssetType.php, app/Domain/Booking/Enums/BookingStatus.php, app/Domain/Pricing/Enums/PricingUnit.php. Two of the three are simple value enums, not transition enums.

No composer package provides a state machine. The workflow mechanisms present are plain Eloquent (app/Models/Workflow.php and app/Models/WorkflowStep.php) for generic approval templates — a database-driven alternative, not a code-driven one.

Only ONE transition graph exists in the whole codebase as a data structure: the $allowedTransitions array in app/Services/BookingWorkflowService.php:14-39. Every other lifecycle is enforced by ad-hoc inline precondition checks.
abstract_state_machine_availability.statement: There is NO generic state-transition abstraction in this codebase to reuse. What exists is one hand-written allowedTransitions array (Booking), three sets of model constants with no guards (Payment, Partner, Settlement), and one unguarded three-state column (booking_media.review_status). The abstract pattern is therefore a FACT OF THE CODEBASE (a protected array plus an in_array check plus a domain exception), not a reusable class.

verdict.decision: DO NOT EXTRACT a shared state-transition framework. Creative should OWN A LOCAL transition pattern, and the pattern should be structurally identical to the one existing instance that works (Booking), not generalised.
reasons: INFERENCE: the sample size is n=1. Exactly one lifecycle in the codebase has a transition graph, and the other five do not. A shared abstraction generalised from n=1 would encode one author's assumptions as a framework, and the five unguarded lifecycles are not evidence of a pattern — they are evidence of no pattern.

INFERENCE: the five existing lifecycles disagree with each other on substance, not just syntax. Booking uses 422 for an illegal transition (app/Domain/Booking/Exceptions/InvalidBookingStateException.php:17); PartnerApprovalController.php:24 uses 400 for the same class of failure; booking_media has no guard at all. There is no consistent behaviour to generalise.

ARCHITECTURE_DOCUMENT: ARCHITECTURE_RULES.md:38 (Rule 6) — 'Avoid blanket repository boilerplate... introduced only where persistence isolation, complex query encapsulation, or testability benefits are demonstrably justified.' The same restraint applies to a transition framework. There is no demonstrable reuse; there is one Creative context.

INFERENCE: extracting a shared abstraction would require touching Booking, which AGENTS.md section 18 forbids as unrelated scope and section 19 forbids as out-of-order debt resolution. The Creative task must not refactor Booking.

INFERENCE: a shared framework would be a new architectural layer in the dependency graph, which AGENTS.md section 7 forbids creating a new layer to avoid a decision, and section 20 forbids as an undocumented guess.
what_creative_should_do_instead: RECOMMENDATION: plain PHP backed enums, one per lifecycle, each with an exhaustive case list — fixing the RST-01 defect where the enum and the model constants disagree. This is the same thing app/Domain/Booking/Enums/BookingStatus.php already does, minus the drift.

RECOMMENDATION: one transition owner class per lifecycle, holding a const TRANSITIONS array keyed by the current state, exactly as app/Services/BookingWorkflowService.php:14-39 does. The class belongs in app/Domain/Creative/<Lifecycle>/, NOT in app/Services/, because it is a pure business rule and must be testable without the container.

RECOMMENDATION: guards in the owner, not in the controller. A method shaped like ->assertCanTransition(from, to) throwing a domain exception. Creative must NOT reproduce the RST-03/RST-04 pattern of precondition checks inline in a controller.

RECOMMENDATION: Laravel Policies for the WHO question ('may this actor perform this transition on this instance'), as recommended in artifact 13 section 8 step 3. Policies and transition guards are orthogonal: the guard answers 'is this edge legal', the policy answers 'is this actor allowed'. Both are needed, and neither substitutes for the other.

RECOMMENDATION: exactly ONE status code for an illegal transition across all nine Creative lifecycles, and a domain exception whose render() emits envelope A (see artifact 14 section 9.3) rather than the fourth envelope currently emitted by InvalidBookingStateException. The render() method is Creative-owned, so this changes no existing behaviour.

RECOMMENDATION: a test that asserts, for every enum case, that the case either appears as a key in TRANSITIONS or is explicitly listed as terminal. This would have caught the RST-01 five-state gap, where 5 model values were neither mapped nor declared terminal.
explicitly_not_recommended: RECOMMENDATION: do not introduce a state-machine composer package (e.g. any workflow/state-machine library). It would be a new dependency, would not match the codebase's zero-extra-dependency posture, and would make the nine Creative lifecycles harder to read in a codebase whose dominant style is a plain array plus in_array.

RECOMMENDATION: do not use the existing database-driven app/Models/Workflow.php + WorkflowStep.php approval-template mechanism. It is designed for configurable, instance-level approval templates; the nine Creative lifecycles are fixed business rules, and a Creative transition has side effects, events and financial effects that a generic template row cannot express.

RECOMMENDATION: do not build a generic StateTransition base class, trait or interface for reuse across the nine lifecycles. They have different actor sets, different side effects, and different financial semantics. The shared part is roughly twenty lines of shape, not behaviour.

concrete_pattern_creative_should_copy.note: This is the shape of app/Services/BookingWorkflowService.php:41-61, restated as a Creative-local class, with the two defects from RST-01 corrected.
concrete_pattern_creative_should_copy.shape: class ProposalTransitionGuard { const TRANSITIONS = [ 'draft' => ['submitted','withdrawn'], 'submitted' => ['accepted','rejected','withdrawn'], 'accepted' => ['declined'], 'rejected' => [], 'withdrawn' => [], 'declined' => [] ]; public function assertCanTransition(ProposalStatus $from, ProposalStatus $to, User $actor): void { if (!in_array($to->value, self::TRANSITIONS[$from->value] ?? [], true)) { throw new InvalidProposalStateException(...); } } }
corrections_to_the_booking_original: The lookup is exhaustive over the enum, so there is no '?? []' silent fall-through. RST-01's defect was precisely that the ?? [] default turned an unmapped state into a terminal state with no diagnostic.

The actor is a parameter, so the authorization question is visible at the call site rather than being answered by a policy class that may not be loaded. The POLICY still decides; the guard only proves the EDGE is legal.
The exception carries a Creative-owned render() that emits envelope A, not the four-key error envelope at app/Domain/Booking/Exceptions/InvalidBookingStateException.php:11-18.

single_status_code_for_illegal_transitio.recommendation: 422 for every Creative illegal transition, on every lifecycle.
single_status_code_for_illegal_transitio.rationale: Booking already uses 422 for exactly this (app/Domain/Booking/Exceptions/InvalidBookingStateException.php:17) and 33 other controller sites use 422 for business-rule violations. PartnerApprovalController.php:24 and :47 use 400 for the same class of failure, which is the minority and the less accurate code — 400 means malformed request, 422 means understood but unprocessable.

every_transition_writes_an_activity_row.recommendation: One append-only activity_logs row per transition, with actor, from-state, to-state and reason.
every_transition_writes_an_activity_row.precedent: App\Models\ActivityLog is already used for exactly this at app/Http/Controllers/Api/RoleController.php:40-49, and booking_activities is the equivalent table for bookings.
every_transition_writes_an_activity_row.rule: ARCHITECTURE_DOCUMENT: AGENTS.md section 10 — financial history is immutable. The activity log is the audit trail that makes the transition graphs in this artifact reviewable after the fact.

no_transition_may_span_a_network_call_un.recommendation: Any transition that dispatches an event, sends a notification or calls a payment provider must commit before the external operation, or isolate it outside the lock.
no_transition_may_span_a_network_call_un.rule: ARCHITECTURE_DOCUMENT: ARCHITECTURE_RULES.md:17 (Rule 4) — 'External network operations must be isolated outside database row locks to prevent connection pool exhaustion and lockTimeouts.' This applies to every Creative transition that fans out a notification.
no_transition_may_span_a_network_call_un.precedent: app/Http/Controllers/BookingController.php:144 dispatches MediaUploaded AFTER the rows are written, which is the correct ordering.

every_financial_transition_is_idempotent.recommendation: Any transition writing to creator_earnings or creator_payouts must be safe to retry.
every_financial_transition_is_idempotent.precedent: 09-...json:563 recommends UNIQUE(project_id, earning_type) as a MANDATORY backstop. There is no request-level idempotency key anywhere in the current codebase (artifact 14 section 10.1).

no_transition_is_authorized_by_a_control.recommendation: Controllers validate the request and delegate. The transition guard proves the edge; the policy proves the actor. Neither may live in a controller.
no_transition_is_authorized_by_a_control.rule: ARCHITECTURE_DOCUMENT: ARCHITECTURE_RULES.md:8 (Rule 1) and AGENTS.md section 6 (controllers stay thin: validate/authorize -> invoke use case -> return response).
no_transition_is_authorized_by_a_control.precedent: app/Http/Controllers/Api/BookingEngineController.php:131 correctly delegates the whole transition to BookingWorkflowService::transition and performs no state check itself — this is the one controller in the codebase that gets it right and it is the model for Creative's /transition endpoint (artifact 14 section 11.5).

discrepancies_vs_existing_artifacts.principle: Source wins. Each item is a place where an existing docs/audit/* artifact is incomplete, wrong, or in conflict with the code, or a finding that no prior artifact records.

items.claim: Sections 52-575 define a status column for every Creative table, and several entries carry explicit status vocabularies (for example :496 'role' OPEN DECISION with proposed final|source|preview|proof).
items.source_reality: The blueprint defines COLUMNS and indexes but no lifecycle: no transition graph, no actor, no authorization basis, no side effect, no event, and no financial effect for any status. An index such as (status, category_id) at :146 is consistent with a state machine and equally consistent with a free-text label.
items.impact: A developer implementing from the blueprint alone would get a status column with unconstrained values. This artifact supplies the missing lifecycle layer, and it is the first artifact to do so.

items.claim: Reusing testimonials for creator reviews is NOT_REQUIRED, and reusing booking_media for deliveries is NOT_REQUIRED, with the reasoning that booking_media's review_status lifecycle 'is an admin approval of an advertiser's ad asset, not a client review of a creator's work'.
items.source_reality: The reasoning is correct but understates the problem. booking_media.review_status has NO transition graph and NO guard at all — RST-03 documents that states are only ever set, never validated, and that the only guard is a BOOKING-state check at app/Http/Controllers/BookingController.php:315. So booking_media is not a weaker version of a Creative lifecycle; it is not a lifecycle.
items.impact: If a Creative developer cites booking_media as the pattern to follow (which the proximity of the two concepts invites), they would copy an unguarded three-state column. LC-DELIVERY must have a written graph.

items.claim: OD-DB-08 is recorded as BLOCKING for the identity model: 'Can a user be both an advertiser (client) and a creator?'
items.source_reality: CONFIRMED as blocking, and the impact is sharper than the blueprint states. Artifact 13 section 3 verifies that RolePermissionChecker resolves a SINGLE slug (app/Support/Authorization/RolePermissionChecker.php:60, :44). A user assigned a 'creator' row in roles would have their buyer role OVERWRITTEN and their buyer permissions REVOKED — not merely under-modelled. The dependency runs both ways: LC-CREATOR cannot be designed until this is answered.
items.impact: D-SM-03 elevates OD-DB-08 from 'a schema question' to 'a question that blocks the entire LC-CREATOR lifecycle'.

items.claim: creator_earnings financial_fields are enumerated, gross_amount = platform_commission_amount + creator_net_amount is asserted as an invariant, and separation of duties for payouts is declared MANDATORY.
items.source_reality: The COLUMNS and the ADDITIVE INVARIANT are sound and are a genuine strength of the blueprint. But no rate, no amount, no currency list and no tax rule exists in any source, and the mandatory separation of duties is currently UNENFORCEABLE: there is no finance role (artifact 13 section 5.6), so creative.earnings.approve and creative.payouts.approve would land on the same role and the control would be vacuous.
items.impact: The blueprint's own invariant is safe to adopt. Its separation-of-duties requirement is not implementable until OD-AUTH-05 is answered. This artifact records the amount, the accrual trigger (OD-SM-09) and the payout mechanism (OD-SM-16) as OPEN_DECISION and proposes no value.

items.claim: settings should gain a 'creative.*' group, e.g. creative.revision_limit, creative.dispute_window_days, creative.payout_minimum.
items.source_reality: None of the three values exists in any rule. Naming a setting key presupposes the rule behind it, and the rule does not exist. The same gap is recorded as OD-SM-08 (revision limits), OD-SM-10 (dispute window), OD-SM-16 (payout minimum) and OD-SM-03 (brief deadline).
items.impact: The three example keys are recorded in this artifact as OPEN_DECISION rather than as proposed configuration. Implementing them would embed invented business rules into a settings table.

items.claim: Reuse roles + role_permissions + RolePermissionChecker + PermissionMiddleware; create no parallel authorization resolver.
items.source_reality: Correct and adopted (artifact 13 section 7.1). The state machine depends on it: the 'actor' and 'authorization_basis' fields of every transition above reference permission strings from artifact 13 section 5, all of which are PROPOSALS and none of which is seeded today.
items.impact: Every transition in this artifact is currently un-authorizable. The dependency chain is: resolve OD-AUTH-01 (dual role) -> seed creative.* permissions -> Creative transitions become authorizable.

items.source_reality: The BookingStatus enum (8 cases) and the App\Models\Booking STATUS_ constants (13 values) disagree on 5 values, and app/Services/BookingWorkflowService.php:45 silently treats an unmapped status as terminal. Verified by reflection. A booking in payment_pending, payment_failed, media_review_pending, expired or refunded cannot be transitioned through the workflow service at all.
items.impact: This is the single strongest argument for the extraction verdict below: the ONE existing transition graph in the codebase is already broken by vocabulary drift between its two owners. It also directly contradicts any assumption that Booking is a model to copy uncritically.

items.source_reality: Illegal transitions are signalled with INCONSISTENT status codes across the codebase: 422 at app/Domain/Booking/Exceptions/InvalidBookingStateException.php:17 and at 33 controller sites, but 400 at app/Http/Controllers/PartnerApprovalController.php:24 and :47, and no guard at all on booking_media.review_status.
items.impact: Creative must pick one. 422 is recommended because it is the majority and because 400 means malformed request. Not recorded anywhere previously.

items.claim: screen_provider_settlements has no currency column and this is a defect Creative must not copy.
items.source_reality: CONFIRMED by source: app/Models/ScreenProviderSettlement.php has no currency attribute, and database/migrations/2026_09_01_000001_create_screen_provider_settlements_table.php defines status/amounts without one. The finding is accurate.
items.impact: RST-06 confirms this while ALSO recording the two things the settlement lifecycle gets RIGHT (the accrual/payout split, and the isPayable predicate at app/Models/ScreenProviderSettlement.php:129) and the one it gets wrong (no edge guards, only state predicates).

items.source_reality: There is a database-driven approval-template mechanism in the codebase — app/Models/Workflow.php and app/Models/WorkflowStep.php — which is a generic state-machine candidate that no Creative audit artifact mentions.
items.impact: It is explicitly REJECTED for Creative in the extraction verdict, on the grounds that it stores configurable approval templates in rows and cannot express a transition with side effects, events and financial effects. Recorded so that the option is visibly considered rather than silently ignored.

open_decisions.statement: Consolidated list. Each states exactly what information is missing. None was resolved, guessed, or worked around. NO amount, percentage, rate, window, limit, deadline, penalty, tax or currency-support statement appears anywhere in this artifact, because none exists in any source.

identity_and_authorization.question: Can a users account be both buyer and creator?
identity_and_authorization.missing_information: A product/identity decision. BLOCKING: it determines whether LC-CREATOR can exist as a status machine at all, or whether creator-ness is derived from the existence of a creator row. Already recorded as OD-DB-08 in 09-...json:698; unresolved. Cross-referenced as D-SM-03.

identity_and_authorization.question: Who holds Creative financial authority?
identity_and_authorization.missing_information: An org decision. There is no finance role, so creative.earnings.approve and creative.payouts.approve cannot be held by different roles and the separation of duties required by 09-...json:611 is unenforceable. Every 'finance' actor field in LC-EARNINGS depends on this.

identity_and_authorization.question: Is the reviewer a distinct role from the buyer, and may the creator review their own delivery?
identity_and_authorization.missing_information: A staffing and internal-control decision. The LC-DELIVERY split between 'approved' (reviewer) and 'accepted' (buyer) is a RECOMMENDATION that assumes they are different actors. If the same actor fills both roles, the approved/accepted split collapses.

financial.question: What exactly triggers a creator earning to accrue, and how is the amount derived?
financial.missing_information: A finance policy. The trigger could be proposal acceptance, delivery acceptance, project completion, or client payment — all four are plausible and none is stated anywhere. The amount basis, the platform share, the creator net, the currency and any tax treatment are equally undefined. This is the single most important unknown in the Creative context. It gates LC-PROPOSAL.accepted, LC-PROJECT.accepted, LC-DELIVERY.accepted and the whole of LC-EARNINGS.

financial.question: What are the earning amounts, the platform share, the creator net, the supported currencies and the tax treatment?
financial.missing_information: A finance policy. NO source states any of these. Existing partner_commissions and screen_provider_settlements values are for DIFFERENT commercial relationships and do not transfer. This artifact deliberately contains no percentage, no currency list and no tax rule.

financial.question: What is the payout minimum, the cadence, and the disbursal mechanism?
financial.missing_information: A finance and operations policy. How money actually leaves the platform for a creator is undefined. 10-...json:1237 proposes a settings key creative.payout_minimum, but the key names a rule that does not exist.

financial.question: Who may reverse a released earning, in which states, and is reversal permitted after disbursement?
financial.missing_information: An internal-control policy. AGENTS.md section 10 mandates the compensating-record mechanism but not the authorisation, the permitted states, or whether a post-disbursement clawback is possible.

financial.question: What is the compensating-record rule when an accepted proposal is later declined?
financial.missing_information: A finance policy: the trigger conditions and the amount for the compensating record. The mechanism is mandated by AGENTS.md section 10; the rule is not.

time_and_limits.question: Does a brief have a submission deadline, and what happens when it passes?
time_and_limits.missing_information: A business rule about time: the duration, the default, and the expiry behaviour (auto-close, stay open, or extend). 09-...json proposes a deadline column and a creative.briefs.extend permission, but no rule.

time_and_limits.question: Is there a limit on how many times a delivery can be sent back for changes?
time_and_limits.missing_information: A business rule: whether a limit exists, whether it is per-round or per-project, and who sets it. Nothing in the codebase or any artifact addresses it.

time_and_limits.question: Is a revision ever auto-accepted after a timeout?
time_and_limits.missing_information: A business rule about time. No SLA or timeout convention exists for any Creative-adjacent action. If it does exist, it implies a scheduled command, which per AGENTS.md section 16 must be framework-registration verified (see RST-07).

time_and_limits.question: Is there an acceptance window after a delivery is submitted, and what happens when it expires?
time_and_limits.missing_information: A business rule about time: the window length and the expiry behaviour (auto-accept, auto-escalate, or remain open). No value is proposed here.

time_and_limits.question: Does a dispute state exist at all, and what is its data model?
time_and_limits.missing_information: A product decision AND a schema decision. Permissions (creative.disputes.open, creative.disputes.resolve) and a settings key (creative.dispute_window_days) are referenced in prior artifacts, but no dispute table and no window rule exist. LC-PROJECT.disputed cannot be implemented without it.

cancellation_and_moderation.question: What happens to in-flight projects, undelivered earnings and pending payouts when a creator is suspended or becomes inactive?
cancellation_and_moderation.missing_information: A product and finance policy. The existing analogue (App\Models\Partner::STATUS_INACTIVE) has no such handling, so there is nothing to copy.

cancellation_and_moderation.question: Who may cancel a brief or a project, at which states, and with what financial consequence?
cancellation_and_moderation.missing_information: A product and finance policy. 09-...json:327 defines a cancelled_by_party COLUMN ('client' | 'creator' | 'admin') but a column is not a rule, and that list omits 'project_manager' entirely. Cancellation penalties are not a concept anywhere in this repository.

cancellation_and_moderation.question: When one proposal is accepted, what happens to the other proposals on the same brief?
cancellation_and_moderation.missing_information: A product rule. The losing proposals need a state that does not imply a buyer action that never occurred.

cancellation_and_moderation.question: When may a client write a review — only after project completion, or at any point?
Are Creative reviews moderated before publication?
cancellation_and_moderation.missing_information: A product decision, and the artifacts CONFLICT: 09-...json:523 proposes is_public boolean default true (no moderation queue) while artifact 13 section 5.4 proposes a creative.reviews.moderate permission (a moderation queue). Both cannot be the design. Unresolved.

cancellation_and_moderation.question: Does a creator's rating have any commercial consequence — rate, ranking, or visibility?
cancellation_and_moderation.missing_information: A product rule. No ranking or rating-weighted behaviour exists in the current marketplace and none is proposed here.

cancellation_and_moderation.question: May a CreativeService carry a monetary rate, and is a published rate binding or indicative?
cancellation_and_moderation.missing_information: A commercial rule. 09-...json:122-148 says a service is offered 'at a defined rate' but states no value, no currency, and no binding semantics.

cancellation_and_moderation.question: Is there a storage quota or any cost associated with holding draft deliveries?
cancellation_and_moderation.missing_information: An operations and cost policy. Nothing in the current storage layer (app/Infrastructure/Storage/LaravelStorageAdapter.php, a single hard-coded public disk) has any quota concept.

architecture.question: Should the per-lifecycle transition guard class live in app/Domain/Creative/<Lifecycle>/ or in app/Services/Creative/?
architecture.missing_information: An architecture decision. This artifact RECOMMENDS the Domain location because a transition graph is a pure business rule and must be testable without the container — but AGENTS.md section 20 forbids guessing, and app/Domain/Creative does not exist yet (AGENTS.md section 8: Creative is 100% greenfield and creating the module root is a Creative task, not an incidental side effect). The nearest nested AGENTS.md for the new directory does not exist.

architecture.question: Should Creative policies be registered in app/Policies/Creative/, and does adding the first policy layer in the repository require an architecture-test change?
architecture.missing_information: An architecture decision plus a test-authorisation decision. tests/Unit/Architecture/ArchitectureRuleTest.php currently pins known violations exactly and would need a new assertion to keep a Creative policy tree from silently absorbing App\Models imports. No test was written and ArchitectureRuleTest was not run, because nothing was changed.

architecture.question: Does the super-admin bypass apply inside a Creative policy check?
architecture.missing_information: An explicit authorization decision, already recorded as artifact 13 OD-AUTH-06 and ARCHITECTURE_RULES.md:43 (Rule 12). A Creative policy does NOT get the bypass that PermissionMiddleware grants, so a super-admin would pass the route and be denied by the policy. This must be settled before the first Creative controller exists, because it is a behaviour decision on a financial-adjacent surface.
